_about: Item 1 (Business) extraction exceptions. 'custom': filers whose 10-K has no usable 'Item 1. Business' heading (annual-report style layouts); a section starts at a line whose whole text matches a 'start' pattern and ends at the next line matching an 'end' pattern (regex, case-insensitive, full line); the first section with 300+ words wins. 'relaxed': tickers allowed the relaxed Item 1 heading rule. Every custom or relaxed extraction must beat that ticker's Yahoo summary on the quality check, or it stays on Yahoo.

C.why: Citi files its annual report as the 10-K: no Item headings in the body; the business is described under 'Overview' (passed the quality check in CI run #5)

MS.why: Morgan Stanley's body headings are 'Business' / 'Risk Factors' without Item numbers (passed the quality check in CI run #5)

GE.why: GE's 10-K has no Item 1 heading in the body and no stand-alone 'About GE Aerospace' line (only in the contents); the business description runs from the end of the contents (its last line is the cross-reference index entry) to 'CONSOLIDATED RESULTS', where MD&A starts (2025 10-K)

HON.why: Honeywell's 10-K replaces 'Item 1. Business' with an 'ABOUT HONEYWELL' section (also a running page header): executive summary, major businesses and the four segments, then MD&A (2025 10-K)

INTC.why: Intel's 10-K is organised by its own sections with a cross-reference index; the business starts at 'Our Business'-style headings (passed the quality check in CI run #5)

MCD.why: The line-start Item 1 rule finds no 300-word section; stand-alone 'Business' / 'General' heading lines work (passed the quality check in CI run #5)

_relaxed_rule: AIG writes 'ITEM 1 | Business'; EXPE's end heading is 'Part I. Item 1A. Risk Factors'. The relaxed rule accepts '|' separators, 'Part I.' prefixes and headings after other text on the line, but the heading must end its line.
